paragraphs.source_en:
The soldiers dreamed that they were blacksmiths, and
Walked out of quarters in somnambulism;
Round the red anvils you might see them stand
Like Cyclopses in Vulcan’s sooty abysm,
645 Beating their swords to ploughshares; — in a band
The jailors sent those of the liberal schism

paragraphs.source_en:
Then freely vp those royall spoyles he tooke,
Yet at the Lyons skin he inly quooke;
But it dissembled, and vpon his head
The Crowne, and on his backe the skin he did,
And the false Foxe him helped to array . . . .
 So he perswaded them, with homage due
Themselues to humble to the Ape prostrate,
Who gently to them bowing in his gate,
Receyued them with chearefull entertayne.

paragraphs.source_en:
The behaviour of the infant Charoba, later Queen of Egypt, in Landor, Gebir (1798) v 117–26, is like-
wise disrespectful of the trappings of monarchy.
 his glorious seat] I.e. royal throne.
 mock-bird] Mocking-bird.
 prone] The context gives the adjective Miltonic overtones. Cp. the devils’ attitude towards Satan in
Paradise Lost ii 477–8: ‘Towards him they bend/With awful reverence prone’.
 somnambulism;] Rossetti 1870; somnambulism, 1824; somnambulism Nbk 16.
 The Cyclops forge iron on anvils in Vulcan’s cave under Etna in Virgil, Aeneid viii 451–3 and
Georgics iv 173–5.
 Around the red hot anvils you might see them stand, MT.
645. Beating their swords to ploughshares] See Isaiah ii 4 and Micah iv 3.
 sent] Written above let canc. in Nbk 16. schism] OED identifies this and the use of the word in PB3
97 as a nonce, meaning ‘a faction, party; a set or class of people’.
